episodes.169095: There were several marine thunderstorm wind gusts in both Galveston Bay and Matagorda Bay.
episodes.169173: As a cold front moved south into the region, the airmass ahead of this was warm and unstable. Storms developed along and ahead of the front and especially from intersecting outflow boundaries and storm mergers. This resulted in some being severe and causing wind damage. Trees and power lines were blown down, but a tornado did occur and cause some structural damage.
episodes.169292: An active monsoon pattern continued across northern and central New Mexico as deep moisture streamed into the area on June 27, 2022. An easterly wave that enhanced convection the previous day was still in the area, again aiding in the development and intensification of afternoon thunderstorms. In Crownpoint, a funnel cloud was spotted for several minutes, but reportedly did not make contact with the ground.
episodes.169352: Monsoon moisture advected north into the region. Residual moisture from previous days convection helped to prime the atmosphere which led to an uptick in shower and thunderstorm coverage across western Colorado. Some storms produced heavy rain which led to localized flash flooding across portions of La Plata County.
episodes.169361: A broken line of thunderstorms moved across this area of the Ohio Valley just ahead of an approaching cold front. While thunderstorms were generally moving fast enough to avoid flooding issues, some locations received multiple rounds of heavy rainfall as multiple convective segments moved across, and in some instances trained across the same area. This led to some isolated instances of flooding in Ohio and Pennsylvania.
episodes.169362: A broken line of thunderstorms moved across this area of the Ohio Valley just ahead of an approaching cold front. While thunderstorms were generally moving fast enough to avoid flooding issues, some locations received multiple rounds of heavy rainfall as multiple convective segments moved across, and in some instances trained across the same area. This led to isolated flash flooding in Ohio and Pennsylvania.
episodes.169487: A line of towering cumulus clouds accompanied a surface trough axis that drifted generally southward across Lake Erie during the late afternoon and early evening of the 27th. Warming and moistening of an unusually-cool low-level air mass over Lake Erie yielded lake-induced instability. Horizontal wind shear along the surface trough axis likely induced surface-based vertical vorticity. This surface-based vertical vorticity was likely ingested by the updraft of a towering cumulus cloud, stretched to tornado-strength via low-level convergence at the base of the updraft, and was then advected upward in the updraft, allowing a waterspout to form offshore Erie County, PA.
episodes.169645: A cluster of storms from a mesoscale convective system that crossed Kentucky moved southwest into East Tennessee in the evening, producing gusty winds that blew down a few trees in the southern Tennessee Valley.
episodes.170007: Prior to the arrival of a prefrontal trough, some thunderstorms managed to take advantage of limited instability in Central New York in the afternoon of the 26th. One thunderstorm over Chenango County became severe and knocked trees and wires down.
episodes.170202: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170241: Daytime heating and an abundance of moisture stirred up afternoon showers and thunderstorms across West Virginia from June 25th to the 27th. The first round of convection on the 25th resulted in several trees down around Central West Virginia while flash flooding took center stage on the 26th and 27th. The town of Flatwoods observed flooding of local businesses as a result of Granny Creek rising out of its banks from all the heavy downpours within passing thunderstorms.
episodes.170586: An inverted trough at 700 mb moved across southern Arizona and with sufficient instability and moisture in place with MLCAPE of around 1000 J/KG and PWAT values of between 1.3 and 1.6 inches, widespread thunderstorm activity was observed across most of south-central and southwest Arizona. Storms first developed across the higher terrain north and east of Phoenix as well as across portions of southern Maricopa County during the early afternoon hours. These storms sent two outflow boundaries from opposing directions, which then collided across the Phoenix metro, sparking the development of additional storms over the Phoenix area. Another cluster of storms then developed across portions of southwest Arizona during the late afternoon into the early evening hours.  No damages or injuries were reported.
episodes.170778: A weak cold front provided focus for thunderstorm development on the afternoon and evening of Sunday June 26. A few of these storms produced strong wind gusts in and near the DFW Metroplex.
episodes.170815: As the dominant upper level ridge began to ease farther off to the west over the Upper Red River Valley on June 26th, a weak upper trough was able to slide south into the region, reinforcing a weak cool front southward. This front encountered a moist and moderately unstable environment as it entered Southwest Arkansas, North Louisiana, and East Texas during the afternoon, with strong forcing yielding the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across these areas. Some of these storms were severe, producing multiple reports of damaging winds and isolated large hail across portions of Southwest Arkansas before exiting the region into North Louisiana.
episodes.170818: As the dominant upper level ridge began to ease farther off to the west over the Upper Red River Valley on June 26th, a weak upper trough was able to slide south into the region, reinforcing a weak cool front southward. This front encountered a moist and moderately unstable environment as it entered Southwest Arkansas, North Louisiana, and East Texas during the afternoon, with strong forcing yielding the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across these areas. Isolated severe storms developed over portions of East Texas, producing a 64 mph wind gust at the Center Municipal Airport in Shelby County and large hail on the Texas side of Texarkana before diminishing during the evening.
episodes.170863: Scattered thunderstorms developed over upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. Several of the storms produced severe weather in the form of brief damaging winds.
episodes.170938: A departing high pressure left the region on the influence of strong warm air advection as a waem front pushed in from the west. When combined with intense surface heating, pockets of high instability began to flourish. Isolated storms developed with a few being on the strong side and ended up producing hail. The largest hail reported was around two inches in diameter.
episodes.170939: A departing high pressure left the region under the influence of strong warm air advection as a warm front moved through as well. When combined with intense surface heating, pockets of high instability began to develop leading to isolated storms developing. A few of the storms ended up producing hail with gold ball-sized hail being the largest.
episodes.171152: Deep monsoonal moisture remained across the region just ahead of an upper trough moving across the southern Rockies.  Storms developed off the eastern slopes of the Sacramento Mountains with some isolated areas receiving heavy rain which caused flash flooding along Highway 130.
episodes.171679: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on June 26. A couple of reports of large hail and wind damage were received.
episodes.171688: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay and Virginia Coastal Waters.
episodes.171690: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.171770: A cold front was moving into south Louisiana on the afternoon of the 27th. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms were moving south along this boundary. The front began to slow its progression and stall as it moved south. It���s common for local summer-time thunderstorms to produce frequent lightning and it was no different for this day. One of those lightning bolts struck a house in Houma, resulting in a fire. No one was home at the time of the fire.
episodes.171833: An Isolated thunderstorm in Buckingham County caused lightning to strike a home.
episodes.171874: Typical summertime showers and thunderstorms produced isolated wind damage and heavy rainfall over the metro Atlanta area on June 27th, with the highest amounts over Atlanta proper and lower amounts stretching east and west along Interstate 20. In DeKalb county, radar estimates indicate that upwards of 3 inches of rain over the area, causing flooding over a portion of Interstate 20 and causing nearby rivers to respond.

This tornado began in a wooded area just east of Greenfield Circle as multiple outflow boundaries collided. Eye witness accounts and videos from the Greenfield Station subdivision, including one from an off duty NWS employee, show strong cyclonic circulation at the cloud base along with a brief tornado that lofted small vegetative debris. The tornado moved southeast along an existing outflow boundary snapping several large tree branches and uprooting at least one tree mainly in a stand of trees between Hollow Oak Lane and Conti Drive. Video evidence shows the tornado quickly gusting out as a surge of outflow from the west quickly catches the tornado. It dissipated while crossing Greenfield Station Road where small branches were snapped by the subdivision pool.

A tornado developed in central Lincoln County near Monticello St NE. Initially uprooting several small trees and larger branches, the tornado traveled south down Rogers Lane NE with an estimated wind speed of 80 mph. The tornado traveled southwest across|Highway 84 E with estimated winds dropping to near 70 mph. As it continued its southwest track, the tornado began to reintensify. Numerous trees were snapped, and a roof was damaged as the tornado crossed Highway 583 SE with winds reaching a maximum speed of 90 mph, EF1 strength. After crossing Highway 583 SE, the tornado continued for several more miles uprooting several more trees and damaging a mobile home before finally dissipating a few miles between Sammy Trail SE and Adolph Lane SE. The maximum estimated wind speed was 90 mph.
